unsupported_claims: In a neural language model, the sequence is ordinary text and the model learns word embeddings from word co-occurrence in sentences.
DeepWalk applies that same skip-gram-style idea to random walks on a graph.
The special language it processes is the "language" of random walks over graph vertices, i.e., sequences of nodes generated by walking the graph.
rationale: The source clearly supports that DeepWalk generalizes neural language models and that it processes a special language composed of randomly generated walks. However, the answer adds extra specifics about ordinary text, word co-occurrence, and skip-gram-style training that are not stated in the provided evidence.
